why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) The quoted sentence exists VERBATIM in env-vars.md, line 425, in the `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` row. The whole line reads: "| `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` | Maximum number of characters in [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) output before truncation (default: 32000, maximum: 160000). When truncated, the full output is saved to disk and the path is included in the truncated response |" — the first sentence supplies the default/maximum the claim cites and the second does not reverse it. (2) The cited code says exactly what was claimed: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:24 `const OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES = 32 * 1024;` and :171-178 `truncateOutput` byte-cuts and appends the bare marker `[Output truncated to 32KB for the parent context.]` — no path, no disk write. Live call site is :236 inside `contentForResults`. (3) The consequence holds independently of the identifier. `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` has 0 hits repo-wide outside the sweep's own data files (rg -a, so NUL-byte files were not skipped); there is no `NESSY_*` analogue; the cap is a module constant with no config or orchestrator-config path (the only `maxOutputBytes` in the repo is the workflow sandbox's, orchestrator/sandbox.ts:28, a different subsystem). No spill-to-disk exists anywhere on this path. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — none touch subagent output truncation. Not a de-brand or dropped-subscription-flow difference either: this is the Pi orchestrator's own subagent tool, which is the fork's Agent-tool equivalent and is active by default. One layer down does soften the claim's wording but not its substance, so the finding survives with a corrected state (see correctedState).
correctedState: Confirmed gap, with one correction to the wording. Our 32 KiB cut at packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:171-178 is hardcoded (`OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES` at :24), is applied only to the inline model-facing text at :236, and its marker carries no file path; there is no disk spill and no env override (`TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` and any `NESSY_*` analogue have 0 non-doc hits repo-wide). But the overflow is NOT simply discarded: the same result block's header prints `agent_id: <id>` (:227, populated for spawned children via spawner.ts:625), and `get_subagent_result(agent_id)` (:690-712) returns the child's result text WITHOUT `truncateOutput`, so the parent has a retrieval handle for the untruncated text — a tool call keyed by agent id rather than the documented file path. That untruncated text is itself host-bounded at `MAX_RESULT_BYTES = 64 * 1024` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:41, applied at :603-605), so output beyond 64 KiB is genuinely lost before it ever reaches the 32 KiB cut. Two further mismatches worth recording: Claude's cap counts characters (32000 default, 160000 maximum) while ours counts UTF-8 bytes (32768), and Claude's is user-tunable to 5x the default while ours is not tunable at all.
